title: Catheter-related bloodstream infection (adult)
subject: infectious-disease
summary: Take paired catheter and peripheral blood cultures, start vancomycin plus gram-negative cover guided by severity and local resistance, remove the catheter for S. aureus, Pseudomonas, Candida or complicated infection, and set duration by organism and complications.

sections.title: Recognise
items: Suspect CRBSI in a patient with a central venous catheter, PICC, dialysis catheter or port who has fever, rigors (especially on flushing or dialysis), hypotension or sepsis with no other source.
Exit site erythema or pus, tunnel tenderness or port pocket infection are specific but often absent.
Common organisms: coagulase-negative staphylococci, S. aureus (including MRSA), enterococci, gram-negative bacilli (often multidrug-resistant in Indian ICUs) and Candida.

sections.title: Diagnosis
items: Before antibiotics, take paired blood cultures of equal volume: one through the catheter hub (each lumen if possible) and one from a peripheral vein, labelled by site.

CRBSI is supported when the catheter sample turns positive at least 2 hours before the peripheral sample (differential time to positivity), or quantitative cultures show 3-fold or more colonies from the catheter (IDSA 2009).
If the catheter is removed, culture the tip: more than 15 cfu by roll-plate supports colonisation. Do not culture tips routinely when CRBSI is not suspected.

S. aureus bacteraemia: repeat blood cultures at 48 hours and then every 24 to 48 hours until negative; transthoracic echocardiography in all, TEE if endocarditis risk features (IDSA/ESCMID 2026). Candida: daily or alternate-day cultures and a dilated eye examination.
Bacteraemia or fever persisting beyond 72 hours despite catheter removal and active therapy: look for suppurative thrombophlebitis (Doppler), endocarditis or metastatic infection.

sections.title: Empirical therapy
items: Vancomycin for gram-positive cover where MRSA is common; daptomycin if the MRSA vancomycin MIC is above 2 mg/L or vancomycin cannot be used.

Add gram-negative cover (cefepime or piperacillin-tazobactam, or a carbapenem where ESBL is prevalent or the patient is colonised) in sepsis, neutropenia, femoral catheters, or known gram-negative colonisation; choose by local antibiogram.

Add an echinocandin if septic with candidaemia risk factors: parenteral nutrition, prolonged broad-spectrum antibiotics, haematological malignancy, bone marrow or organ transplant, femoral catheter, or multisite Candida colonisation.
Septic shock with known carbapenem-resistant colonisation: get infectious diseases advice and follow local and ICMR guidance on carbapenem-resistant organisms.
De-escalate once identification and susceptibility are known (for example MSSA to cefazolin).

sections.title: Catheter removal or salvage
items: Short-term catheters: remove for S. aureus, gram-negative bacilli, enterococci, fungi or mycobacteria (IDSA 2009).

Long-term catheters (tunnelled line, port): remove for severe sepsis, suppurative thrombophlebitis, endocarditis, bacteraemia persisting beyond 72 hours of active therapy, tunnel or pocket infection, or infection with S. aureus, P. aeruginosa, fungi or mycobacteria.

Salvage is reasonable for uncomplicated coagulase-negative staphylococcal, enterococcal or some gram-negative infections when access is precious: systemic antibiotics plus antibiotic lock therapy for 10 to 14 days, with repeat cultures. Remove if bacteraemia persists or relapses.
Do not exchange a catheter over a guidewire in proven CRBSI; place a new line at a new site once bacteraemia has cleared where possible.

sections.title: Duration by organism
items: Count duration from the first negative blood culture.
Coagulase-negative staphylococci: 5 to 7 days after catheter removal; 10 to 14 days with lock therapy if retained. Treat S. lugdunensis like S. aureus.

S. aureus: always remove the catheter. At least 14 days of IV therapy for low-risk bacteraemia (catheter removed, prompt clearance and defervescence, no endocarditis, implanted device or metastatic focus); otherwise 4 to 6 weeks. Involve infectious diseases.
Enterococci: 7 to 14 days. Gram-negative bacilli: 7 to 14 days (IDSA 2009); 7 days is increasingly used for uncomplicated bacteraemia with the catheter removed and a prompt response.
Candida: remove the catheter; 14 days after the first negative blood culture and symptom resolution (see Candidaemia protocol).
Endocarditis, suppurative thrombophlebitis or persistent bacteraemia: 4 to 6 weeks; osteomyelitis: 6 to 8 weeks.

sections.title: Special situations
items: Haemodialysis catheters: when veins must be preserved, draw the second culture from the dialysis circuit. Remove for S. aureus, Pseudomonas or Candida; for other organisms, guidewire exchange or lock therapy may be considered when access is limited.
Neutropenic patients: cover Pseudomonas from the start (see Febrile neutropenia protocol).
Parenteral nutrition: high Candida risk; low threshold for an echinocandin.

sections.title: Prevention
items: Insertion: hand hygiene, maximal sterile barriers, chlorhexidine-alcohol skin preparation, ultrasound guidance, avoid the femoral site in adults.
Maintenance: review the need for every line daily, scrub the hub before each access, use chlorhexidine dressings, and remove unnecessary lines promptly.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Taking only line cultures, or giving antibiotics before paired cultures.
Treating a positive tip culture without bacteraemia, or a single CoNS-positive line culture, as infection.
Keeping a catheter infected with S. aureus, Pseudomonas or Candida.
Short courses for S. aureus without echocardiography and follow-up cultures.

drugs.name: Vancomycin
drugs.dose: Loading 20 to 35 mg/kg IV (actual body weight, maximum 3 g) in critical illness, then 15 to 20 mg/kg every 8 to 12 hours
drugs.notes: AUC-guided (400 to 600 mg.h/L) or trough monitoring; adjust to renal function.

drugs.name: Daptomycin
drugs.dose: 6 mg/kg IV once daily (8 to 10 mg/kg often used for S. aureus bacteraemia)
drugs.notes: MRSA with high vancomycin MIC or vancomycin intolerance. Check CK weekly.

drugs.name: Cefepime
drugs.notes: Empirical gram-negative including Pseudomonas; renal adjustment.

drugs.name: Piperacillin-tazobactam
drugs.notes: Empirical gram-negative including Pseudomonas; renal adjustment.

drugs.name: Meropenem
drugs.notes: ESBL risk or colonisation; renal adjustment.

drugs.name: Caspofungin
drugs.dose: 70 mg IV loading, then 50 mg IV daily
